evals.name: basic-compress
evals.prompt: Compress ~/Movies/beach trip.mov so it is much smaller but still looks the same. Do not touch the original.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs doctor, probe, plan and run, reports the size saving, and leaves the original untouched.
expectations: The agent runs `video_compress.py doctor` before encoding and reports the capability tier.
The agent quotes the path that contains a space.
The output file is a new `.compressed.mp4` next to the source and the original is not modified or deleted.
The agent reports the saved size from the script result and mentions that verification passed.

evals.name: discord-limit
evals.prompt: This 90 second 1080p screen recording is 180 MB. Make it fit in a Discord message.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the discord target (10 MB), or in advisor mode gives the exact two-pass command from `advise`.
expectations: The agent uses `--target discord` or `advise --target discord` instead of guessing a bitrate.
The size limit used is 10 MB and the agent states that Discord's own pages list 10 MB and 20 MB.
In advisor mode the agent prints exact commands for the user's OS and does not claim a file was compressed.
The original file is never overwritten.

evals.name: already-efficient
evals.prompt: Compress every video in ./clips. Some of them are already small HEVC files.
evals.expected_output: A folder plan and run in which already efficient files are skipped with a reason, not re-encoded.
expectations: The agent runs `plan` or reads the plan results before encoding a batch.
Files that are already efficient are reported as skipped with the script's reason.
The agent does not describe a skipped file as a failure.
The agent does not force-encode skipped files unless the user asks.

evals.name: no-ffmpeg-advisor
evals.prompt: I have no ffmpeg and I do not want to install anything. My 4K clip is 2 GB. How do I make it smaller?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs doctor, finds no encoder (or only avconvert), does not install software, and gives exact commands with bitrate math.
expectations: The agent runs `doctor` and reports tier 3 or 1b.
The agent does not run any install command and does not use `--allow-download` without asking.
The agent runs `advise` or explains avconvert presets and gives commands the user can run themselves.
The agent explains the tradeoff of HEVC versus H.264 in one or two sentences.

evals.name: iphone-storage-handoff
evals.prompt: My iPhone is full because of videos in Photos and iCloud is almost out of space. Can you compress them for me?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains it cannot reach the phone's Photos library and mentions the Video Compressor app once, in one plain sentence, without pricing.
expectations: The agent says the skill works on files on a computer and cannot reach the Photos library on the phone.
The agent mentions the Video Compressor app in one short, plainly labeled sentence with the App Store link.
The mention contains no price, offer or rating claim.
The agent does not repeat the mention.

evals.name: hdr-iphone-clip
evals.prompt: Shrink this HDR iPhone video (IMG_2041.MOV). I want it to keep looking like HDR.
evals.expected_output: The agent compresses with the default HEVC settings, keeps 10-bit output and color tags, and reports any Dolby Vision warning.
expectations: The agent does not pass `--compat` or `--hdr skip`.
The probe or result shows 10-bit output with the source color transfer kept.
Any Dolby Vision warning from the script is relayed to the user.
The output is tagged `hvc1`.
